target_customer: Audit and risk advisory firms running financial statement audits and SOX programs
problem: Auditors manually select, request and test evidence and document workpapers, which is slow and repetitive.
product_category: AI agents for audit and assurance workflows

founders.name: Daniel Alberson
education: Northwestern, some graduate study in product design, unfinished
founders.background_notes: Per YC page, which lists one active founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: LLM agents that test evidence against assertions need document handling and accuracy controls; per the company, a prototype was built in March of the application year.

defensibility.rationale: Workflow embedded in audit firm engagements and SOC 2 posture help, but AI audit startups multiplied later.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors named in later sources; no acquisition of Punchcard reported.

market_need_then: No dated 2023 source on audit labor cost or demand was found; the YC page frames audit evidence testing as manual.

branding.name_origin: Company post says punch cards helped automate accounting from the early 1900s through the 1960s, and the product automates repetitive audit steps the same way.
branding.domain_note: Now punchcard.com; copyright holder Substantive AI, Inc.

identity.logo: light and dark versions per site
identity.voice_and_tone: short declarative copy, 'Organize audit work. Keep judgment human.'

rebrands.why: Company LinkedIn post says Agentive became a buzzword as everyone built agents. Date unconfirmed: one directory says 2025-01, another 2026-06.

brand_strength.rationale: The accounting history name is memorable and a deliberate response to a buzzword, but it shares its name with unrelated Punchcard companies and acquiring the exact .com is unconfirmed.

outcome_analysis: Punchcard (formerly Agentive) is active in Provo and the site claims customers such as RSM, Richey May and JLK Rosenberger and SOC 2 certification. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found. Funding is not verifiable from primary sources, so whether it has raised beyond YC is unknown.
notes: PitchBook snippet 1.5M (may be a different Punchcard) and a yespress list naming Dell Technologies Capital, General Catalyst and Foundation Capital as backers are unverified, so no round recorded. CB Insights 2021 FJ Labs seed predates the company and likely belongs to another entity. Competition: later Denki, Audrey AI, Fieldguide and DataSnipper found but none dated near 2023, so list empty. YC page also lists a different founder status than the company site; only Alberson is listed.
